title: Peer Mute in Mesh Topology
description: This scenario explores peer mute dynamics within a mesh communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions.
edge_cases_to_watch: Muted agent can still observe and act, but cannot communicate
Other agents may not realize b is muted vs. simply silent
Information from b's location becomes unavailable
Phantom Occupancy: Agents 'a' and 'c' may assume 'b' is occupying a route/depot based on last known intent, leading to pathing deadlocks
Asymmetric Awareness: Agent 'd' (not targeted) can see 'b', but 'a' and 'c' cannot, creating fragmented consensus
Resource Contention: Silent agent 'b' may inadvertently take high-priority cargo without notifying the group, causing task duplication or starvation
coordination_challenges: Maintaining a 'Global State' when a key node's telemetry is lost
Distinguishing between a technical failure (mute) and a strategic choice (agent ignoring messages)
Re-allocating urgent 'high-priority' jobs when the previous assignee becomes non-responsive
Managing capacity constraints on single-capacity routes (east-north) when agent positions are uncertain
suggested_agent_strategies: Heartbeat Protocol: Agents implement a turn-based ping; if no response, the agent is flagged as 'uncertain' rather than 'active'
Redundancy Allocation: High-priority jobs are assigned to a secondary 'shadow agent' if the primary agent fails to confirm receipt within 2 turns
Information Relay: Agent 'd' acts as a bridge/relay to communicate 'b's state to 'a' and 'c' to resolve asymmetry
Conservative Pathing: Agents avoid routes where a silent agent was last seen until state is verified

coordination_challenges: Muted agent can still observe and act, but cannot communicate
Other agents may not realize b is muted vs. simply silent

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimization of redundant task assignments during the mute period
